subtitle: Quintet · Super Nintendo Entertainment System

body: Soul Blazer is Quintet's Super Nintendo action role-playing adventure about restoring a world whose living souls have been imprisoned. The player controls a warrior sent by the Master to defeat monsters and release the people, animals and plants held inside their lairs. Settlements begin empty and gradually return to life as the surrounding dungeons are cleared. The reward for fighting is therefore visible outside the battlefield: another resident appears, a building returns or a familiar place acquires somebody who can explain what should happen next.

Destroying a monster lair releases a particular soul and reconnects it with the place it belongs. Returning to town reveals the result, and the restored inhabitant may provide advice or an item needed elsewhere. The player moves repeatedly between the dangerous area and its recovering community. Each side gives the other a purpose. A corridor leads toward the next person to rescue, while a conversation back home explains why another part of the dungeon has become important or how it can finally be crossed.

The warrior can communicate with many kinds of living things, making a dolphin or a flower part of the adventure's social world. That broad idea of restoration gives the changing settlements their character. Sword fighting, equipment and magical assistance support the immediate action, while Yukihide Takekawa's music accompanies the different regions. Released by Enix in 1992, Soul Blazer developed Quintet's interest in making the recovery of a place playable. Its central satisfaction comes from returning somewhere that was empty and finding life waiting there because of the last journey.
